TO:  MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  JUDY SMITH, CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT – OCTOBER 2011

Status Report

This report reflects the status for FY 2011-12 through the first four months of the fiscal year.

General fund revenues are 3% below expected, while total operating revenues are 7% below
expected. Slow revenue performance for the first four months is offset somewhat by development
fees, which are currently tracking at 20% above expected. We have seen projects with significant
plan check valuations, which will hopefully translate to building permit fees in the near future once
projects enter the construction phase. There are no specific areas of concern within revenue
performance as most categories below expected are related to timing of receipts. As an example,
due to accrual and disbursement schedule, October performance reflects two months receipts for gas
taxes, even though we have concluded four months of the fiscal year.

Total operating expenditures are at expected levels (0% deviation). Individual department results
vary with the Police Department currently 6% below expected and General Government 5% below
expected, due to the administrative reorganization and current staffing compared to budget. It is
expected the Police Department will track more closely to budget because as of the end of October
the department is at full staffing for sworn officers (25 positions). This is the first time, in a very
long time that all sworn positions are filled, with three new officers at various stages of their field
training. General government performance will continue to show savings throughout the balance
of the fiscal year. Public Works is running 18% ahead of expected. This is due to one-half payment
of our annual PV Transit obligation, as well as work associated with warm weather for the Streets
and Parklands departments; this year involving street tree trimming (66% of budget expended).

Spot Report

None

TO:  JUDY SMITH, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  ALEXA D. DAVIS , ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  PALOS VERDES TENNIS CLUB FY 2012 OPERATING
  AND CAPITAL BUDGETS AND RESOLUTION R11-37;
  APPROVING A $5 INCREASE IN MONTHLY DUES

DATE:  NOVEMBER 8, 2011

ISSUE

Shall the City Council review and approve the FY 2012 Palos Verdes Tennis Club (PVTC)
operating and capital budgets?

BACKGROUND AND ANALYSIS

The Palos Verdes Tennis Club fiscal year begins on January 1 and the concession agreement
requires that the Club submit their budget to the City for review. The PVTC Board of Directors
approved the 2012 budgets at its October meeting. On November 2nd, Council liaisons Bird and
Perkins met with Treasurer Bruce Merchant, incoming Treasurer Tom Liesy and Manager John Hall
to review the budget.

2011 Projected Results:

The 2011 budget was based on 387 members and assumed a net income of $670, with revenue at
$510,130 and expenditures at $509,460. Based on actual performance as of September 30, 2011,
the Club projects an operating loss of $15,715 on revenue of $506,330 and expenses of $522,045.
This loss is due to fluctuations in membership throughout the year (although currently at 400
members, membership dipped to ~378), and budget deviations within Administrative Expenses
(salary, benefits, grounds, office). Salaries increased in order to offset rising benefit cost to
employees, while benefits decreased due to employee insurance plan changes. Grounds and office
expenses increased due to unanticipated costs associated with the removal of dead pine trees and
publication of an all-member directory necessitated by a large change in membership. Another area
of deviation comes from the program side (lessons, juniors), which is customary from year to year.
Program revenue and expenditures generally offset each other and are considered in each year’s
budget as such.
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  8
 2012 Operating Budget:

The budget reflects estimated net income of $2,805 on revenue of $532,205 and expenses of
$529,400. Both revenues and expenditures reflect a 3.2% increase compared to projected 2011
year-end. There is a $5 dues increase proposed for 2012. Dues are proposed to be $70/month for
resident $85/month for non-resident effective January 1, 2012. In anticipation of losing a small
amount of membership due to the modest dues increase, the 2012 operating budget is based upon an
assumption of 390 members, which is ten less than current membership. The last dues increase
occurred in 2006 (+$10/month). In the 2012 budget, dues ($343,800) and guest fees ($9,600)
represent 50.5% of total operating revenue.

The challenge for the Club in this budget, as in the past several years, will be meeting the slim
operating margin after three years of an incrementally increasing deficit. The Club believes its
healthy cash balance of $355,704 (including capital funds of $105,837), equal to 67.2% of the
proposed operating budget, is more than sufficient to cover an unanticipated operating shortfall and
that a $5 dues increase is appropriate at this time.

2012 Capital Budget:

The Club anticipates a beginning capital balance of $115,591. The proposed capital budget
assumes income (initiation fees) of $36,000 and expenditures of $48,000 for an ending balance (12-
30-12) of $103,591. Expenditures include an extensive court resurfacing (hydro blasting) of courts
11 & 12 at an estimated cost of $7,500/court. Two additional projects for 2012 were planned for
FY 2011 but were not completed. These include court fence painting ($19,500) and windscreen
replacement ($15,500). The Club has expressed that court fence painting is an expensive and timely
process and therefore may be postponed to another future year. The Club additionally sets aside
$40,000 of its capital balance for potential roof replacement, in the case of an emergency.

Also, due to the cash position, liaisons suggested the Club consider a long term capital needs plan
which could be discussed at a mid-year meeting in 2012. The City Council liaisons will provide an
additional verbal report on their meeting. There is currently no waiting list for Club membership
and the Club offers an installment plan for payment of the initiation fee that make membership
easily affordable.

ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  Approve the FY 2012 Palos Verdes Tennis Club operating and capital budgets and adopt
  Resolution R11-37; approving a $5 increase in monthly dues.

2.  Decline to approve the FY 2012 operating and capital budgets. This would require the Club
  and Board of Directors to change the budgets to address City Council concerns.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  9
 RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council approve the Palos Verdes Tennis Club FY 2012 Operating
and Capital Budgets and adopt Resolution R11-37; Approving a $5 increase in monthly dues.

BUDGET IMPACT

The PVTC is a non-profit entity whose budget is separate from the City’s. The PVTC pays a 10%
concession fee on gross revenues (dues, guest fees, and food and beverage sales) to the City. The
Club’s FY 2012 budget includes a cost of $35,700 for payment of these fees to the City.

TO:  JUDY SMITH, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  ALLAN RIGG, PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH PSOMAS FOR ADDITIONAL
  GROUNDWATER INVESTIGATION SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $14,400

DATE:  NOVEMBER 8, 2011
_____________________________________________________________________________

The Issue

Should the City Council approve a contract amendment with Psomas to perform additional groundwater investigation
services in and around Malaga Cove Plaza and approve Resolution R11-36 adjusting the Fiscal Year 2011/12 budget in
the amount of $14,400?

Background and Analysis

Groundwater within and around the Malaga Cove Plaza has been a significant issue for many years. Over time there
has been an increase in the number and frequency of sinkholes caused by water intrusion into underground utilities, as
well as electrical failures due to water filling underground electrical facilities. A subdrain built in the alley behind
Malaga Cove Plaza in 1997 has been found to be near the end of its useful life. Recent measurements in the monitoring
wells show that the groundwater is at all-time highs, probably due to the rains late last year.

On March 22, 2011 the City Council awarded a contract to Psomas in the amount of $66,300 for the investigation of
groundwater in and around Malaga Cove Plaza. The intent of the study was to determine the source of the groundwater,
how the groundwater moved into and through the Plaza, and potential means to reduce the groundwater. The contract
amount included $20,700 for the installation of three monitoring wells.

Staff worked with Psomas to identify locations for the three groundwater monitoring wells and they were recently
installed to the southeast, southwest, and south of the Malaga Cove Plaza. A number of findings have been developed
including the occurrence and movement of groundwater in the Malaga Cove Plaza area. These findings include:

  •  Groundwater predominantly occurs in a sand layer that rests atop of the underlying bedrock (Altimira
  Shale);
  •  Groundwater levels in groundwater monitoring well VC-1 (immediately south of Malaga Cove Plaza)
  have shown a correlation between heavy precipitation events and peak groundwater levels with a time
  lag of approximately 3-4 months;
  •  Preliminary data suggests that the sand is present on the terrace that underlies Via Campesina and
  may thicken toward the east-southeast;

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  11
   •  Towards the west beneath Via Del Monte, the sand is present but does not contain groundwater (at the
  present time) although data collected suggests that historically the sand contained groundwater;
  •  The upper terrace beneath Via Pinale (immediately south of the library) did not contain the sand and
  groundwater was not encountered in the bedrock (shale);
  •  The sand to the southeast increased in thickness to about 10 feet and groundwater appeared to be at a
  higher elevation suggesting groundwater movement from the east;
  •  Reconnaissance of the creek immediately east and south of Via Campesina did not indicate that the
  sand was present or in contact with the sand and gravel bottom of the creek, indicating that this is not
  a major route for the groundwater to flow from the south.

The groundwater levels south of Malaga Cove Plaza seem to indicate that the groundwater may originate toward the
southeast. Psomas believes that two additional wells and groundwater level monitoring are needed to the east-southeast
of Malaga Cove Plaza to confirm the origin of the water. Psomas has designated that the location of the new wells
would be near 2575 and 2625 Via Campesina as shown on the attached exhibit.

In addition, groundwater level monitoring devices would be placed in these new wells to measure effects on
groundwater levels from precipitation in the area. If groundwater is originating in this area the lag time should be
shorter than what is being observed at Malaga Cove Plaza. The importance of this is that if the origin of recharge for
the groundwater contained in the sand can be ascertained and if it results from recharge from the creek bed east of Via
Campesina, then a potential long-term cost-effective remedy could be formulated to reduce/eliminate the source of
groundwater.

Staff believes the wells are needed to continue the study and confirm the flow of the groundwater. It is good news if in
fact the water is coming from the east as it would support the concept of extracting the groundwater for irrigation at the
golf course prior to flowing down to the Plaza.

Alternatives Available to Council

The following alternatives are available to the City Council:

1.  Approve an amendment to the contract with Psomas for additional groundwater investigation services and
  approve Resolution R11-36 adjusting the Fiscal Year 2011/12 budget in the amount of $14,400.

2.  Deny an amendment to the contract with Psomas for additional groundwater investigation services professional
  services agreement.

Fiscal Impact

As the Fiscal Year 2011/12 capital budget did not anticipate the need for the additional funds for this project, we have
prepared Resolution R11-36 adjusting the Fiscal Year 2011/12 budget in the amount of $14,400 to be funded from the
unobligated capital fund balance.

Recommendation from Staff

Staff recommends that the Council approve an amendment to the contract with Psomas for additional groundwater
investigation services and approve Resolution R11-36 adjusting the Fiscal Year 2011/12 budget in the amount of
$14,400.

Staff report prepared by:
Allan Rigg
Public Works Department

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

  November 8, 2011

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:50 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Rea. The Pledge of
Allegiance followed.

ROLL CALL:  Council Members Humphrey, Perkins, Goodhart, Mayor Pro Tem Bird,
  and Mayor Rea

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  City Treasurer Sherwood, City Attorney Hogin, Assistant City Attorney
  Smith, Asst. to City Manager Davis, Executive Asst./Deputy City Clerk
  Kroneberger

MAYOR’S REPORT – Matters of Community Interest

Mayor Rea reported that a 30-second National Emergency Alert System test will occur at 11:00
a.m. on Wednesday, November 9.

Mayor Rea announced that Planning Director Rigg will conduct an educational forum on Planning
Department processes on Thursday, November 17, at 7:00 p.m. in Council Chambers of City Hall.
City staff and a PVHA representative will be present to answer questions.

Mayor Rea announced the SBESC/SCE Holiday Light Exchange will take place at the City Hall e-
Waste Drop-Off area on PVDW, on Wednesday, November 30, from 1:00-5:00 p.m. Incandescent
light strings may be exchanged for new energy efficient LED lights; available to SCE customers.

CONSENT AGENDA (Items #1 - 3)
It was moved by Council member Humphrey, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bird and unanimously
approved that the following Consent Agenda items (except for Council Minutes of October 25,
2011; Council members Goodhart and Perkins recused) be approved:

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 25, 2011

  MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT – OCTOBER 2011

NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  1
   ACTIONS OF JOINT CITY COUNCIL, PLANNING COMMISSION, AND HOMES
  ASSOCIATION MEETING OF NOVEMBER 1, 2011

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC – No one came forward to speak.

NEW BUSINESS

PALOS VERDES TENNIS CLUB FY 2012 OPERATING AND CAPITAL BUDGETS AND
RESOLUTION R11-37 APPROVING A $5 INCREASE IN MONTHLY DUES

Mayor Rea recused himself from discussion, citing potential conflict of interest; he turned the gavel
over to MPT Bird and left the Chamber.

Assistant to City Manager Davis reported for FY 2011, the PV Tennis Club projects an operating loss
of $15,715 (revenue of $506,330; expenses of $522,045) due to fluctuations in membership
throughout the year and budget deviations within Administrative Expenses (salary, benefits,
grounds, office). She said the 2012 budget reflects an estimated net income of $2,805 on revenue of
$532,205 and expenses of $529,400. A $5 dues increase is proposed ($70/month, residents;
$85/month, non-residents) effective January 1, 2012. The 2012 operating budget is based upon an
assumption of 390 members, which is ten less than current membership. The last dues increase
occurred in 2006; this is the third year the club is running at a deficit and a $5 dues increase is
needed at this time.

The Club has a healthy cash balance of $355,704, equal to 67.2% of the proposed operating budget,
which is more than sufficient to cover an unanticipated operating shortfall.

For FY 2012, a beginning capital balance of $115,591 is anticipated. The proposed capital budget
assumes income from initiation fees of $36,000 and expenditures of $48,000 for an ending balance
(12-30-12) of $103,591. Expenditures planned include extensive resurfacing of two courts, court
fence painting ($19,500), and windscreen replacement ($15,500). The Club has expressed that
court fence painting is an expensive and timely process and may be deferred to a future year.
$40,000 of the Club’s capital balance is set aside for potential roof replacement in the instance of an
emergency.

Asst. Davis stated that due to the Club’s cash position, liaisons suggested a long term capital needs
plan which can be discussed at a mid-year meeting in 2012. Currently, there is no waiting list for
Club membership. She said the Club offers an installment payment plan for membership initiation
fee: new members are required to make a $200 down payment and $35 is added to each month’s
dues for residents; $45 per month for non-residents, which works well for members and the Club
alike. She noted the installment plan was incorrectly reflected on the accompanying resolution,
confirming with Council member Humphrey that this was the only change reflected on the modified
resolution for Council’s consideration.

CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  2
 Councilmember Goodhart confirmed with John Hall, PVTC General Manager, that a majority of the
wind screens will be replaced this year, because it has been deferred for several years; however,
they can defer painting of the fences as they appear to be holding up well. Councilmember
Goodhart noted that pro shop sales were down. Mr. Hall explained that they have no inventory
costs; the Club receives 15% of sales for items sold, which is stocked by an outside contracted
source. Also, there is zero net to the Club for lessons. Mr. Hall concluded that the Club is as busy
as it’s ever been, noting that less is being spent on luxury services such as lessons; however, play is
not down.

Councilmember Perkins, in her first year as Tennis Club liaison, noted she had been concerned
about the multi-year deficit and if the $5 increase would be adequate, but concerns were allayed
upon review of capital needs and the need to take a more long term look. She remained concerned
about the cost of utilities—costs for lighting are considerable and suggested Asst. Davis can work
with the Club to decrease those expenses. She supported the recommendation as presented.

Councilmember Humphrey noted club membership is a bargain for the price at the City’s beautiful
facility. She supported approval of the budgets and $5 rate increase.

Councilmember Goodhart said in light of having no increase in dues for six years, he could support
the modest $5 increase and budgets as presented.

Mayor Pro Tem Bird congratulated the management and leadership of the Club, increasing its
membership to 400, keeping expenses down, and noted that the cash reserves balance is good.

On motion of Councilmember Humphrey, seconded by Council\member Perkins, City Council
approved the FY 2012 Palos Verdes Tennis Club operating and capital budgets, and adopted
Resolution R11-37, as amended, approving a $5 increase in monthly dues, by unanimous oral vote;
Rea recused.

Mayor Rea returned to the Chamber.

AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH PSOMAS FOR ADDITIONAL GROUNDWATER
INVESTIGATION SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $14,400

Public Works Director Rigg reported that groundwater within and around the Malaga Cove Plaza
has been a problem for many years. A subdrain built in the alley behind Malaga Cove Plaza in 1997
is near the end of its useful life. Recent measurements in the monitoring wells show that the
groundwater is at all-time highs.

On March 2011, Psomas was awarded a contract for the investigation of groundwater in and around
Malaga Cove Plaza; three monitoring wells were drilled. They have found that there is a correlation
from heavy rainfall accumulation and irrigation has minimal impact to the groundwater occurring in
the Plaza. The westerly and south well have no groundwater; the well at Via Chico shows a
significant amount of groundwater flowing from the east, potentially through the golf course.

CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  3
 PVGC is doing their own investigation into using groundwater for irrigation purposes. Extracting
the groundwater would have a downstream effect and potentially impact Malaga Cove Plaza.

Director Rigg said Psomas is asking for additional funding to add two additional easterly wells at a
cost of $14,400 to confirm the origins of the groundwater, which includes drilling, installation and
monitoring.

Councilmember Goodhart asked why Psomas was not considering locating a well at Via Segunda or
Elevado (SE) because of an apparent gap between wells.

Michael Donovan, Psomas hydrogeologist, explained the provided geological map and the presence
of water bearing sand focused on Malaga Cove Plaza, impermeable shale on the upper terraces, and
lack of sand on the upper tiers; sand being their primary focus. On Via Campesina, two wells are
planned, and possibly a third well at Pinale Lane. If they can prove recharge is occurring at the
east/southeast, they can eliminate it (or turn it off) through a variety of techniques to reduce the
amount of water that is coming into the sand causing drain failure. Roots from trees are also
infiltrating drain systems.

Councilmember Goodhart confirmed with Mr. Donovan that a creek runs along and crosses over
Via Campesina and will be further investigated. Mr. Donovan said there is no indication this area is
a slide zone and the investigation will be about a one-year process. City Manager Smith stated any
well at the Golf Club would not be drilled by the City. Councilmember Goodhart queried as to
water rights at Golf Club. Director Rigg said the City has the water rights at the Golf Club, but it
could be extracted with City’s authorization.

Mayor Rea asked what mitigation measures could be taken if it is determined this is a recharge
situation. Mr. Donovan said one option is to inject concrete creating a grout curtain so water cannot
come through, or reduced significantly; channelization of the creek is another potential option.

Councilmember Perkins asked when they could expect results from Psomas. Mr. Donovan said
they need a full season for investigation; a wet season is forecasted, so results could potentially be
presented in August 2012.

Councilmember Humphrey asked what the cost would be if a third well is needed. Director Rigg
there would be no additional cost; only a total of two wells would be drilled and installed,
depending on what’s found in the field.

On motion of Councilmember Humphrey, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bird, City Council approved
an amendment to the contract with Psomas for additional groundwater investigation services and
adopted Resolution R11-36, adjusting the FY11-12 budget in the amount of $14,400 by unanimous
oral vote.

STAFF REPORTS

CITY TREASURER’S REPORT
CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 8, 2011
  4
  PRESENTATION ON CITY’S INVESTMENT POLICY AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE

City Treasurer Sherwood reported that the City is fiscally sound, with a reserve balance of ~$7 million.
He reported that the investment portfolio is primarily with low-risk LAIF (Local Area Investment
Fund) and U.S. Government securities. He said there is ~$6 million invested outside of LAIF,
returning an average of 1.75%, which amounts to $105,000 annually. Treasurer Sherwood said we
operate under the ‘prudent person’ rule; following Civil Code guidelines. Our investments are made in
US Government securities or LAIF, the safest, most liquid, and secure. All of our investments have
maturity dates of 5 years or less. It is not anticipated interest rates would go up sooner. Under
authority of Resolution R94-22, the City Treasurer is authorized to manage the City’s investments,
upon discussion with the City Finance Director and City Manager. He said the custodian for our funds
is Union Bank.

Councilmember Goodhart asked why a local bank cannot be utilized. Treasurer Sherwood responded
they don’t have all the services we require, which are offered by Union Bank.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Smith reported that representatives of Southern California Edison have committed to
installation of fault indicators (narrows geographic focus for repairs) and 10 fuse switches (so smaller
areas would be affected in the event of outages) by the end of the year to assist in ameliorating the
ongoing problem of power failures in the City, and pursuant to the most recent occurrence in Lunada
Bay. SCE will present a report to Council in December.

Councilmember Goodhart reiterated residents’ frustration and asked if the City can address this issue
with the Public Utilities Commission. Councilmember Perkins said individuals can file complaints
with the PUC. City Manager Smith said the City has heard from Lunada Bay residents who have
started that process.

Director Rigg said another process provides for customers to file claims with SCE when damage
occurs to power surges.

Councilmember Goodhart said the problem is the aging infrastructure and it was his hope SCE would
return with a planned solution.

DEMANDS
